question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping's entrenched position within the Chinese Communist Party's leadership structures drives the 95.5% trader consensus against removal before 2027. He has appointed most members of the Politburo Standing Committee and Central Military Commission, with no scheduled party congress, term expiration, or formal succession process until autumn 2027. Recent public activities, including speeches on economic planning, AI governance, and commemorations in mid-2026, alongside ongoing military purges that further centralize authority, reinforce continuity. Realistic shifts remain possible through sudden health developments, elite-level consensus for early transition amid major crises, or unforeseen internal challenges, though these lack current institutional triggers or evident momentum.

Trader consensus prices Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Gavin Newsom, and Jon Ossoff as the narrow leaders due to their respective appeals—AOC channeling progressive energy as a potential Bernie Sanders successor, Newsom positioning as a high-profile Trump critic with strong fundraising networks, and Ossoff drawing support as a Senate standout in a battleground state. Kamala Harris trails despite advantages with Black voters and the South Carolina primary slot, while a broad group of governors and senators competes for the center-left lane. The tight spread stems from the distant timeline, absence of definitive polling or endorsements, and uncertainty over primary calendar effects and midterm outcomes. Separation could emerge from formal announcements, early fundraising hauls, or shifts in voter sentiment ahead of the 2028 primaries.
